review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.summary: Orchestrator's `ares.*` subscription DLQ-loops every non-Envelope message forever

evidence: orchestrator/main.rs:139 subscribes `ares.*`, which matches ares.dlq, ares.activity and ares.vulns; main.rs:69-75 republishes every unparseable payload to SUBJECT_DLQ unconditionally — a message received ON ares.dlq that fails Envelope parsing is republished to ares.dlq and re-received, with no exit condition

Non-Envelope traffic is routine: ActivityEvent JSON from four agents and vuln advisories both fail `serde_json::from_slice::<Envelope>` (missing id/correlation_id/source/kind/payload), so every routine activity event enters an infinite DLQ republish cycle — unbounded bus amplification at the central router

delivery_count (main.rs:120-127) reads a `Nats-Delivery-Count` header nothing ever sets on core-NATS publishes, so MAX_DELIVERIES=3 can never trip; the documented 'drop only on ares.dlq after 3 deliveries' contract (docs/services.md:48) is inert
Self-republish of routed envelopes is guarded (main.rs:90 `msg.subject.as_str() == subject`) but no equivalent guard exists for ares.dlq or for non-Envelope subjects
detail.suggestion: In handle_message, return early when `msg.subject` is SUBJECT_DLQ or is not one of the routed ingress subjects (or subscribe only to `ares.alerts` plus explicit command subjects); before any DLQ republish, write an `ares-dlq-count` header and drop when it exceeds MAX_DELIVERIES — that makes the documented 3-delivery contract real and kills the loop.

review::.::holistic::api_surface_coheren.summary: api-server returns three different error-body shapes (plain text, typed ACP error, empty) despite one documented contract

Only the kill-switch handler emits an `error` key (crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:66-70), and it adds a `path` field no other endpoint has.

review::.::holistic::authorization_consi.summary: Every service uses one owner Postgres role; no RLS anywhere and the audit chain is never verified

evidence: The blind packet reports 7 tables (a2a_tasks, agent_checkpoints, bas_results, response_actions, seen_alerts, tool_idempotency, vuln_advisories) and zero with RLS; each table is created ad hoc by whichever service owns it (e.g. crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:207-230, crates/tool-server/src/idempotency.rs:125-133).
Every service connects with the same DATABASE_URL (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:236-248, crates/api-server/src/main.rs:334), so any of them can UPDATE or DELETE audit_log rows the others wrote.
crates/audit/src/lib.rs:59-115 writes prev_hash/hash but no code anywhere re-walks the chain to detect tampering (no reader beyond api-server's plain SELECT at crates/api-server/src/main.rs:187-197).
infra/helm/ares/templates/postgres.yaml provisions a single POSTGRES_USER with no per-service roles.
detail.suggestion: Create per-service Postgres roles at bootstrap with GRANT INSERT/SELECT only on audit_log (no UPDATE/DELETE) and enable RLS on the per-run tables keyed by service role, then add a verify() that re-walks audit_log hash links and expose it through GET /audit so tampering is actually detectable.

SELECT that derives prev_hash from the last row) so the chain stays linear; note the single-writer assumption in the docstring otherwise.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::dry_ru.summary: `Tool::execute -> Result<Value>` returns Ok for a dry run, so an unconfigured backend reads as a successful action

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:35-37 `dry_run()` returns `Ok(json!({"dry_run": true, "args": args}))`, and every executor falls back to it when its credential is missing (:88-91, :110-113, :145-148, :170-173, :211-214, :377-383, :408-410).
crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:193-198 maps any `Ok` to `ToolResult { ok: true, error: None }`, so the gateway (agent-core/src/gateway.rs:93-95) and the agent loop see an ordinary success.
crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:290-313 then runs `post_check` and records a rollback entry for an action that never happened.
detail.suggestion: Return an enum from `Tool::execute`, e.g. `enum ExecOutcome { Performed(Value), DryRun { args: Value } }`, and map `DryRun` to a non-success `ToolResult` (or an explicit `skipped` field) so callers cannot mistake 'backend not configured' for 'action performed'.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::gatewa.summary: A transport/parse failure on /invoke is synthesized as DecisionKind::Deny and persisted as a policy verdict

:290 treats that as `denied`, :298-307 persists `"decision": invoke.decision.kind` into `response_actions.result`, and :326-330 emits "denied by policy; recorded" to the activity feed.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::cvss_m.summary: CvssMetric fields are non-Option but parse_cve fills them with ""/0.0, and 0.0 is itself a valid CVSS score

evidence: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:813-826 declares `version: String, source: String, kind: String, vector: String, base_score: f64` with no `Option`, promising fields the NVD payload may omit.
crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:1056-1063 fills them with `unwrap_or("")` / `unwrap_or(0.0)`, so 'absent' and 'empty'/'0.0' are indistinguishable at the type level.
crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:100 filters `m.base_score > 0.0`, which drops a genuine CVSS 0.0 (severity None) record and cannot distinguish it from a parse default.
detail.suggestion: Type the genuinely optional parts as `Option<String>`/`Option<f64>` (or have `parse_cve` skip a metric when `cvssData` is missing) and let callers decide the policy for an absent score instead of encoding absence as 0.0.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::persis.summary: a2a/acp write protocol states as SQL literals and re-parse with lossy fallbacks instead of using the enums

evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs writes `'working'` (:418), `'failed'` (:442), `'canceled'` (:486-487) and `'completed'` (:337, :617) while `TaskState::as_str()` (a2a/src/task.rs:44-53) is the canonical mapping and is only used for display (:441 in acp.rs, run_event).

crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:316 reads back with `TaskState::parse(&row.state).unwrap_or(TaskState::Submitted)`, so an unrecognised stored value becomes a live 'submitted' task that a client can re-drive.

crates/acp/src/lib.rs:172-182 maps every unknown status to `InProgress` (a completed run could be resurrected), and crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:85,452 keeps the same literals in the DDL and the cancel UPDATE.
detail.suggestion: Bind `TaskState::as_str()`/`RunStatus::as_str()` in the SQL statements, propagate parse failure instead of defaulting (`?` on the `Option` or `BackendError::Internal`), and add a CHECK constraint listing the enum's values so the TEXT column cannot drift from the enum.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::rollba.summary: Rollback plans are untyped JSON naming tools that are absent from the allowlist and never validated or executed

evidence: crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:104-129 returns `Option<Value>` built with `json!({"tool": …, "args": …})`, naming `blocklist.ip.remove`, `wazuh.active_response.unisolate_host`, `entra.user.enable`, `ad.user.enable`, `firewall.rule.remove`, `o365.email.release`, `misp.ioc.unblock`.
None of those names appears in policies/tools.yml (the allowlist ends at `siem.index.delete`), so the recorded rollback could never pass policy.
The value is written to `rollback_json` (:315-323) and no code path reads it back, so neither a type nor a test can catch the mismatch.
detail.suggestion: Introduce `struct RollbackCall { tool: ToolName, args: Value }` (or reuse `ToolCall`) built only from allowlisted names, and assert at startup that every rollback target is in `PolicyEngine::tool_names()`; if rollback execution is not planned, drop the column instead of recording unusable plans.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: ActivityEvent is serialize-only, so every consumer filters activity payloads as untyped JSON

crates/api-server/src/run_stream.rs:62-71 and 157-168 parse each ares.activity payload into serde_json::Value and compare v.get("workflow_run_id").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some(corr) plus v.get("step"), restating the type's field names in two places.

review::.::holistic::abstraction_fitness.summary: NatsSink's publish policy is bypassed by publish_activity and by bas-runner's local publish helper

detail.suggestion: Route vuln-agent's case creation through HttpToolGateway::invoke_allowed("thehive.case.create") so kill switch, policy and audit apply uniformly; keep response-agent's summary write only if it is documented as bookkeeping, otherwise add a policy-gated tool for it. review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::audi.summary: Audit hash uses nanosecond timestamp, verification re-hashes the microsecond DB value

evidence: lib.rs:103-109 builds the canonical string with `ts = ts.to_rfc3339()` where `ts = Utc::now()` (nanosecond precision), then hashes it.

The same `ts` is bound into a `timestamptz` column (lines 111-128); PostgreSQL/sqlx store microseconds, so the value read back differs from the hashed one whenever the sub-microsecond digits are non-zero.
verify_chain (lines 161-180) recomputes the canonical string from the stored `row.ts.to_rfc3339()`, so it reports `broken_at` with 'hash does not match row contents' for essentially every intact row.
detail.suggestion: Truncate the timestamp before hashing and storing, e.g. `let ts = Utc::now().trunc_subsecs(6)` (or hash `ts.timestamp_micros()`), so the canonical string is identical on insert and verify.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::gate.summary: Non-2xx /invoke responses become a synthetic 'deny' policy verdict

evidence: gateway.rs:85-106 builds `Decision { kind: DecisionKind::Deny, reason: "gateway returned {status}: {body}" }` for any non-success HTTP status, so a 502/503/504 is reported as a policy denial.

review::.::holistic::logic_clarity::resp.summary: Kill-switch halt breaks the loop and then reports 'done' with a Final checkpoint

main.rs:345-356 then publishes `done` ('{n} actions executed') and `save_final_checkpoint`, which writes `Step::Final`.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::shar.summary: Shared SSE state machine takes a concrete PgPool, so the module both protocols depend on cannot be unit-tested

evidence: `run_stream.rs:34` `checkpoint_progress(pool: &PgPool, ..)`, `:94` `RunRecord::load(pool: &PgPool, ..)` and `:121` `activity_stream(rx, pool: PgPool, ..)` bind the replay/close state machine to `sqlx::PgPool`; the file has no test module.
`wait_for_terminal` (run_stream.rs:55-82) needs only a `broadcast::Receiver` and a timeout — lag handling, wrong `workflow_run_id`, and terminal-step matching are all testable today but untested.
The codebase already has the better pattern in `agent-core/src/checkpoint.rs:22-40`: a `CheckpointStore` trait plus `InMemoryCheckpointer`, which is why `agent_loop.rs` tests need no Postgres.
detail.suggestion: Replace the `PgPool` parameter with a small trait or a record-loader closure so `activity_stream` can be driven by a fake, and add direct tests for `wait_for_terminal` (lagged receiver, non-matching correlation id, terminal vs non-terminal step, timeout).

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::acti.summary: `terminal_step` agent/step string contract has no test; renaming one emitted step silently hangs every SSE stream

evidence: `activity.rs:30-38` is a hard-coded agent x step table ('close', 'handoff', 'kill_switch', 'done', 'deployed', 'rejected'); the module has no `#[cfg(test)]`.

`run_stream.rs:72` is the only thing that closes an A2A/ACP stream, and the emitters are per-agent literals in triage-agent, response-agent, detection-agent and hunt-agent — a rename on the emitting side degrades to `wait_for_terminal` timing out (run_stream.rs:81) instead of a failing test.

detail.suggestion: Add a table test over every agent x terminal step plus a non-terminal step and an unknown agent, and a test asserting each agent's emitted step constants are members of that table (export the literals as consts so the test can reference them).

evidence: `idempotency.rs:183` `Store::pg` and `:188` `Store::mem` are documented as 'identical semantics', but all 9 tests (lines 424-545) drive only `mem` and the pure `Record` helpers; `claim_pg`'s `INSERT .. ON CONFLICT` reclaim/expiry SQL (lines 217-320) is never executed.

`audit/src/lib.rs:157` `verify_chain` and `:238` `canonical_string` (the exact string whose hash is stored) are untested — the two tests cover `sha256_hex` shape and `GENESIS_HASH`, so a field-order change in `canonical_string` would invalidate every existing row's hash with no failing test.

`orchestrator/src/dedupe.rs:32` `check_and_mark`, `agent-core/src/checkpoint.rs:49` `PostgresCheckpointer` and `api-server`'s `a2a_tasks`/`acp_runs` lifecycle have no tests; `grep -rn 'sqlx::test|testcontainers' crates` returns nothing.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::agen.summary: Agent loop's kill-switch branch and two of three budget stop reasons are never exercised

evidence: `agent_loop.rs:142-148` blocks a tool call and stops with `kill_switch`; the three tests (lines 239-275) cover only `final`, `max_steps` and fence stripping.
`budget.rs:39` `exceeded_reason` is pure and takes an injected `Instant`, yet has no direct test, so the `max_tokens` and `wall_time` stop reasons are never asserted anywhere.
`gateway.rs:130-155` `invoke_verdict`'s retry loop (retryable flag, `MAX_RETRIES`, `backoff`) is untested — only the sleep helper in connectors has a bound test.

`hunt-agent/src/main.rs` has zero tests: `score_hits` (line 64) is pure bucketing; `orchestrator/src/main.rs:49` `route_subject` (the routing table where the fixed DLQ-loop bug lived) is untested while `dedupe_key` next to it is tested.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::eval.summary: The only end-to-end evaluation of the LLM triage layer is a JSON format check

evidence: `evals/run.sh` validates that each golden-set line parses and carries label tp/fp, then prints `TODO: replay golden sets through triage-agent and score precision/recall (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)` and exits 0; CI runs it as the `eval` job, so a green build says nothing about verdict quality.
The corpus is 13 alerts (`evals/golden_sets/triage_seed.jsonl`) and `evals/policy_tests.md` (34 lines) is a prose negative matrix that no test executes.
Nothing exercises `triage-agent`'s `process` (main.rs:393) end-to-end; its only entry point is `main()`, so prompt/verdict/threshold regressions are invisible until runtime.
detail.suggestion: Make `run.sh` replay the golden set through a testable `triage_agent::process` (extract it from `main`, drive it with `MockProvider` or recorded completions) and fail below a precision/recall threshold; convert the `policy_tests.md` rows into cases in `policy-engine/tests/policies.rs`, which already loads the shipped policy files.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::dry_.summary: Unconfigured executors' dry-run success and its propagation to response-agent have no test

evidence: `executors/mod.rs:35` `dry_run(args)` returns `{"dry_run": true}` as a *successful* result, used by the `DryRun` struct (lines 551-563, 12 allowlist entries) and by every connector-backed executor whose client is `None` (e.g. `OpensearchQuery::execute`, lines 66-70); `tool-server/src/main.rs:192-199` lifts that into `ToolResult.dry_run`.

`response-agent/src/main.rs:283` and `:300` skip the post-check and the rollback exactly when `dry_run` is set — the only guard that stops a credential-less fake success from being recorded as a real action — and neither side is asserted by a test.
`tool-server/src/main.rs:180` `run_tool` is DB-free, but only the happy `cvss.score` path is tested (main.rs:347-366).
detail.suggestion: Add a tool-server test asserting `run_tool` returns ok=true + dry_run=true for a connector-less tool (e.g. `thehive.case.create` with `ConnectorConfig::default()`) and ok=false for an unregistered name; add a response-agent test that `rollback_for` is not attached for a dry-run result.
